title: [130] Windows GPU transcription: add GPU-capable whisper-cli and an installer choice CPU / GPU-Nvidia
why_we_need_this: On Windows, transcription always runs on CPU even with a working Vulkan GPU driver, so it is much slower than it should be. Checked on a machine with an NVIDIA RTX 4060 (driver 581.15) and Intel UHD 750: vulkaninfo finds the RTX 4060 as DISCRETE_GPU, the bundled vulkan-1.dll (1.4.357.0) matches the system one, yet `whisper-cli.exe --help` prints no "ggml_vulkan: Found N Vulkan devices" banner. Root cause: the pinned official `whisper-bin-x64.zip` (whisper.cpp v1.8.4, downloaded by @server/src/scripts/setup.ts) is a CPU-only build. @whisper/bin/win-x64 has no ggml-vulkan.dll, ggml.dll is 67 KB, and no binary contains any Vulkan string. The comment in setup.ts and project-context claim ggml-vulkan.dll is statically linked into ggml.dll; that is wrong. The diagnostics page then says "Whisper engine operational" while the log blames the driver ("no GPU driver with Vulkan support"), which misleads users. The problem is not installer-specific; it affects every Windows build, dev included.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A GPU-capable Windows x64 whisper-cli exists for NVIDIA cards: choose and justify the build (CUDA/whisper-cublas, or Vulkan built with -DGGML_VULKAN=1); document the choice and the installer size/runtime cost of each. The current official CPU-only whisper-bin-x64.zip stays as the CPU variant.
2. The NSIS installer has a new page "Speech recognition engine" with two options: "CPU" (default, preselected) and "GPU - NVIDIA". No other vendor options now; the page must be easy to extend with more options later (AMD/Intel).
3. The choice is persisted for the Electron main process (e.g. a small file in %APPDATA%\August, like model-dir) and survives updates/reinstalls; electron/src/main.ts points WHISPER_BIN_PATH to the matching variant (bundled in resources, or downloaded on demand if bundling makes the installer too large - state which and why).
4. The installer verifies its own work, as with model-dir: it reads the persisted choice back and shows a clear warning if it could not be saved or the chosen variant files are missing. The user must never need to inspect logs. All $APPDATA access runs in the "current user" shell context (an all-users install otherwise writes to C:\ProgramData).
5. If GPU-NVIDIA is chosen but no usable NVIDIA driver/GPU is found at runtime, whisper still transcribes on CPU automatically (AUG-116/117 fallback) and the diagnostics page says so in plain language. The installer must not block or crash.
6. Diagnostics text and the startup log distinguish "no GPU backend in this build" from "no driver found"; the false claim about a statically linked ggml-vulkan.dll in @server/src/scripts/setup.ts and project-context/transcription/whisper-setup is corrected.
7. @server/src/scripts/setup.ts fetches or builds both variants reproducibly (pinned versions, SHA256), stays idempotent, and electron-builder extraResources still bundle what is needed.
8. On the RTX 4060 dev machine: a fresh install with "GPU - NVIDIA" shows the GPU in /api/health (gpuBackend) and a real transcription runs measurably faster; record CPU vs GPU time on the same audio in the task result. A fresh install with the default "CPU" behaves exactly as today.
9. The uninstaller and silent installs behave sanely: silent install (/S) uses the default CPU; uninstall removes the persisted choice file.
10. Installed NSIS build verified end to end for both choices.
important_constraints: Both platforms matter: macOS uses Metal, has no such installer page, and must not change. Keep the CPU fallback and the --no-gpu retry logic (gpuBackend.ts). Keep the bundled Khronos vulkan-1.dll loader and license for the CPU variant if it still needs it. Installer size growth must be reported. The installer page order must keep working in per-user and all-users mode (see installer.nsh customWelcomePage/customInit/customInstall patterns). Out of scope for now: AMD/Intel options; add them only on a later request.
